foundry_blurb: This early design from 1988 sat undigitised for decades before finally becoming Coroner.

name: Dracula
classification_notes: Genuine fraktur blackletter construction with heavy swash and ligature detailing.
summary: A swash-heavy fraktur blackletter named after the most famous vampire in fiction.
description: Dracula leans hard into blackletter drama, with a huge set of ligatures and swashes and a separate Inline companion cut. Five weights, plus a variable font version, run from Light to Black.
foundry_blurb: Blackletter remains the sharpest way to radicalise a piece of typographic expression, and Dracula takes that idea to its most theatrical extreme.

name: Dream Within A Dream
classification_notes: Broken, angular strokes place this with the blackletters, even though its curling flourishes give it a strong ornamental, Art Nouveau character.
summary: An ornamental blackletter built for decadent artists and named after Poe's poem.
description: Dream Within A Dream mixes broken gothic strokes with curling Art Nouveau flourishes, styled for exhibition catalogues and other decadent-minded printed matter. It comes in a single, elaborate weight.
foundry_blurb: Decadent artists need a special typeface for their exhibitions and catalogues, and this one was built with exactly that crowd in mind.

name: Hexenrunen
classification_notes: The letterforms are monolinear and geometric rather than broken fraktur strokes, so this sits with the display faces despite its witchy, blackletter-adjacent name and Storm's own blackletter tag.
summary: A geometric, runic-looking display face named after German witch runes.
description: Hexenrunen was originally intended for an obscure electronic music project that never saw the light of day, and its monolinear, angular caps read more like invented runes than true blackletter. It comes in a Regular and a mirrored Reverb cut.
foundry_blurb: This one was originally meant for a certain obscure electronic music project that, in the end, never got released.

name: Julinka
classification_notes: True broken fraktur blackletter construction, with unusually thorough diacritic support for the genre.
summary: A fraktur blackletter designed for the type designer's own daughter.
description: Julinka was made for Storm's daughter, with particular care given to how diacritics behave within a blackletter structure. Five weights, from Light to Black, plus a variable font, give it real range for a genre that is often single-weight only.
foundry_blurb: Made for the designer's daughter, with the instruction to enjoy her own gothic style, and font use in the real world remains the most interesting stage of a typeface's life.

name: Monarchia
classification_notes: A true fraktur blackletter revival of a historical Rudolf Koch design, elegantly calligraphic in structure.
summary: A digital revival of Rudolf Koch's Frühling, dressed with modern OpenType swashes.
description: Monarchia is Storm's digital rendering of Frühling, the historic blackletter originally drawn by German designer Rudolf Koch, brought up to date with swashes, alternates and ligatures as proper OpenType features. It comes in Regular, Bold and a Text cut for smaller sizes.
foundry_blurb: This digital rendering of Rudolf Koch's Frühling adds swashes, alternates and ligatures as OpenType features.

name: Moyenage
classification_notes: True broken blackletter construction, built out into a full weight and width superfamily.
summary: A broken gothic superfamily named after the French for the Middle Ages.
description: Moyenage takes its name from the French moyen-âge, and by 2026 has grown into a proper superfamily: six weights across six widths, from Ultra Condensed to Ultra Expanded. It carries a stylised, angular medieval character throughout.
foundry_blurb: Moyenage has just turned eighteen this spring, a fully grown medieval bachelor of a typeface by now.

name: Moyenage Sans
classification_notes: Explicitly the sans-serif companion to the blackletter Moyenage family, so classified as sans-serif despite the shared name and medieval concept.
summary: The sans-serif companion to Moyenage, keeping its medieval flavour without the broken strokes.
description: Moyenage Sans reinterprets its blackletter sibling as a clean sans, described by Storm as an experimental project suited to music packaging, invitations and offbeat lettering. Nine weights across nine widths make it one of the foundry's largest sans releases, with genuine Cyrillic support built in.
foundry_blurb: Where the calligraphic Moyenage family suits shorter texts and posters, this sans-serif variant is more experimental, built for record covers, odd inscriptions and invitations.

name: Plagwitz
classification_notes: Full fraktur blackletter alphabet in a single dense weight.
summary: A dense fraktur blackletter named after Leipzig's book-craft quarter.
description: Plagwitz takes its name from the Leipzig district that hosted the 2000 ATypI Congress at its book-craft museum and workshops, a fitting home for a proper fraktur revival. It comes in a single, richly detailed weight.
foundry_blurb: Plagwitz is named after the part of Leipzig where the Werkstätten and Museum für Buchkunst are found, once host to the 2000 ATypI Congress.

name: Spiritist
classification_notes: Storm's own description confirms this as a monolinear blackletter, stripped of the usual stroke contrast but still built on calligraphic bones.
summary: A monolinear blackletter reduced to its pure geometric skeleton.
description: Spiritist keeps blackletter's calligraphic, round-nib pen structure but strips away the usual contrast, leaving naive, simplified forms that stay legible at almost any size. Five weights, from Thin to Black, add swashes and decorative endings for festive use.
foundry_blurb: Blackletter is usually known for contrasty, sharp-edged shapes with a certain emotional weight, but here the aim was to follow its pure schematic skeleton instead, landing on naive, simplified forms that read clearly at any size.

name: Wittingau
classification_notes: True gothic blackletter construction, accompanied by a matching ornamental symbols font.
summary: A blackletter named after the German name for the South Bohemian town of Třeboň.
description: Wittingau pairs a proper gothic text structure with a companion Symbols font of floral ornaments, evoking the monastic and herbal history of the region around Storm's own studio. Three weights, Regular, Medium and Bold, cover the main alphabet.
foundry_blurb: Wittingau is the old German name for Třeboň, the beautiful South Bohemian town near the designer's own studio.
